fields.text: Turn a color illustration into a printed black-and-white manga panel: clean ink lines, solid black fills and screentone dots instead of color. Muse paints the color art here; swap it for a 📷 Image input to convert your own picture. Qwen Image 2.1 Edit does the conversion in one pass. Inspired by the ComfyUI-MangaScreen node by @renrenrenz5cq that went around X this week (https://x.com/renrenrenz5cq/status/2110357826745098659) and @studiomasakaki's Qwen + MangaScreen recipe (https://x.com/studiomasakaki/status/2111473583835004974).

A full-color anime-style comic illustration with clean cel shading and bold outlines: a small cartoon fox with orange fur and a white chest, wearing a yellow raincoat with the hood up, holds a glowing red paper lantern and walks along a narrow rainy old-town street at night. Wet cobblestones reflect warm lantern light, a cat sleeps on a windowsill, laundry hangs on a line overhead, a tiny bridge over a canal in the background, falling rain streaks. Strong light and shadow, dramatic low camera angle, full body, family-friendly, no text, no signs with letters, no speech bubbles.

Redraw image 1 as a printed black-and-white manga panel. Keep the exact composition, camera angle, character pose and every background element in the same place.
Ink: clean black line art with varied line weight, crisp outlines.
Blacks: the darkest areas become solid black ink fills.
Tones: every mid-tone becomes screentone, a pattern of round halftone dots; darker areas get bigger, denser dots and lighter areas get smaller, sparser dots.
Highlights: the lantern glow and its reflections stay clean white paper.
Rain: thin straight ink strokes.
Pure black and white only: no color, no smooth grey gradients, no added text, no speech bubbles, no sound effects.
